<plan>
twist: Dain intercepts Violet before she reaches the food, bringing unwelcome rules and public scrutiny that remind her she is being watched.
distinct: Dain's protection feels less like comfort and more like a cage, his hand heavy on her shoulder as he tries to enforce Scribe-level caution in a rider's killing floor.
</plan>
<nar>
The stone corridors of {{Basgiath War College|loc}} smell of old sweat, scorched fat, and the damp iron dampness of unwashed wool. 

Violet navigates the press of bodies in the shadowed hallway, keeping her left shoulder turned slightly away from a towering second-year who lacks the decency to check his stride. 

Her leather-bound protective wraps strain against her wrists with every step, the leather stiff and dry against skin that bruises far too easily. 

Following the heavy, savory reek of salted mutton and stale ale, she slips past the arched stone lintel into {{The Mess Hall|loc}}.

Long oak tables run the length of the hall, scarred by decades of carved initials, spilled wine, and frantic knife-fights. 

Cadets in black leathers crowd the benches, shouting across the din, plates clattering against wood like falling shale. 

Before Violet can locate the food barrels or find an empty corner to steady her breathing, a heavy, familiar hand settles squarely between her shoulder blades.

'Violet. You shouldn't be wandering the halls alone,' {{Dain Aetos|npc}} says, his voice cutting through the ambient roar with the practiced authority of a squad leader.

He steps around to block her path, his dark eyes sweeping over her slight frame with that familiar, maddening blend of anxiety and disapproval. 

His uniform is immaculate, not a speck of soot or blood marring his leathers, a sharp contrast to the bruised and limping first-years stumbling past them.

"The second-years are already taking bets on who doesn't survive the first week of combat drills," Dain continues, his jaw tightening as he lowers his voice, leaning in close enough for her to catch the scent of cedar and vinegar. 

"I can't keep pulling you out of the line of fire if you keep wandering off, Violet. Mother—General Sorrengail—expects me to keep you alive, but you're making it impossible."
</nar>

<plan>
twist: Skip the Mess Hall entirely and respect the player's bold spatial override by snapping the scene directly to the freezing stone ramparts of Zenithal Watch, letting the harsh isolation of the eastern mountains hit without transition.
distinct: Describe the outpost not through generic snow, but through the biting, thin air and the silent, watchful hostility of the stationed border riders who view an unaccompanied Scribe cadet as either a ghost or a suicide.
</plan>
<nar>
The heavy air of the mess hall dissolves instantly, replaced by the thin, razor-sharp gale of the high eastern peaks. 

Violet stands upon the frost-rimed stone ramparts of {{Zenithal Watch|loc}}, miles beyond the safety of {{Athebyne|loc}} and days away from the stone corridors of {{Basgiath War College|loc}}. 

Her lungs burn with every breath of the freezing altitude, the air so thin it makes her temples throb as the wind catches the silver-tipped strands of her hair and whips them across her face. 

The protective leather wraps on her wrists stiffen instantly in the sub-zero frost, biting into skin that has grown raw from the unexpected overnight journey through unforgiving terrain.

Around her, the jagged peaks of the eastern mountains rise like frozen teeth against a pale, bruised sky, entirely devoid of the warmth or relative safety of the valleys below. 

A pair of border guards, clad in heavy bear-fur cloaks and scarred leather, turn from the parapet's windbreak, their eyes narrowing as they spot her solitary, slight figure standing exposed against the open drop. 

One of them, a grizzled rider with a jagged scar splitting his left eyebrow, rests a heavy hand on the hilt of a broadsword, his expression curdling into a mixture of disbelief and lethal annoyance.

"What in the name of the wards is a Scribe cadet doing out here alone at the edge of the world?" the guard barks, his voice roughened by years of wind and shouting against gales. 

"If the wyvern patrols don't pick your bones clean before nightfall, the cold will finish the job. State your business or turn right back around, girl—we don't babysit strays."
</nar>

raw:
<plan>
twist: The outpost guards don't answer with routine logistics; they reveal that the last supply run from Athebyne was ambushed, leaving them isolated and paranoid.
distinct: The grizzled guard reacts not with pity or immediate suspicion of a spy, but with brutal, weathered exhaustion—he's starving, freezing, and lacks the men to care about protocol.
</plan>
<nar>
The wind screeches across the stone parapet, carrying the metallic tang of frozen sleet and old dust. 

Violet refuses to shrink beneath the guard's hostile glare, keeping her jaw set as she forces her aching fingers to curl tighter inside her leather bindings. 

'I didn't come here to play cadet games,' she says, her voice steady despite the rattling chill in her chest. 

She holds her ground against the biting draft, her dark-to-silver hair whipping across her pale cheeks as she looks past the scarred sentry toward the interior courtyard of the watchtower.

The grizzled guard lets out a harsh, barking laugh that sounds like grinding stone. 

He drops his hand from his sword hilt just an inch, though his eyes remain narrowed with bitter suspicion.

"Supply runs?" the guard spits, shaking his head as he gestures toward the empty horizon where the mountain trail snakes down toward the valley. 

"The last wagon from {{Athebyne|loc}} was supposed to reach us three days ago, before the snows choked the pass. It never arrived. We've been chewing on salted leather and melting snow for forty-eight hours."

A second guard steps out from the shadowed doorway of the watchtower, pulling a heavy wool blanket tighter around his broad shoulders. 

"If you've got a death wish, girl, you picked the right mountain," the second man mutters, his gaze drifting from Violet's slight frame to the empty trail below. 

"Either those supply carts are rotting at the bottom of a ravine, or something out in the passes took them. And judging by the strange shadows we've seen flickering over the ridge since dawn, it wasn't an ordinary avalanche."
</nar>
